clues.text: Under the law given through Moses, every native-born Israelite had to live in these for seven days.
God had Israel live in these each year so later generations would know how He housed them leaving Egypt.
Moses taught that the feast tied to these began on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, after the harvest.
Ezra and the family heads, studying the Law in Jerusalem, found that Israel was to live in these.
In Ezra's day, people were told to fetch olive, myrtle and palm branches from the hill country to build these.
After the exile, Jerusalem's people built these on rooftops and by the Water Gate and the Gate of Ephraim.
When the returned exiles lived in these, Israel had not celebrated that way since the days of Joshua son of Nun.
